If you are going to be removing it more often there are external cases you can buy (be sure that you pick one that supports a capacity that is useful to you). There are also docking bays that you can put an internal drive into and remove more easily then opening a case. You can also buy drives already in an external case as a package though these tend to cost more, and can come with software to help automate backups or may just suck to use. If this is something for a business you may look into other options for routine backups for example tape drives allow for a cheaper per media price but with an upfront cost for the drive.

At the end of the day an important thing to remember if you are going to transport hard drives, especially traditional spinning disk drives is don't bounce them they have moving parts and can be damaged by being dropped something to protect them if you are clumsy is a plus, they can also be damaged banging into each other as they have a circuit board on the bottom and metal corners that could crack it so one case with many floating in it can be as bad as no case.

Also look into what your use is going to be and the drive you are buying, in my example I picked something cheap high capacity. Some are made for constant use some are made for intermittent use and using them as not designed can shorten the lifespan or reduce reliability.

Always remember it is good to have a backup plan but without a restore plan it is useless, plan how you will restore the data and test periodically to ensure that both the backup is working and that you can restore from it either without the other has no benefit.
